strings.name: Andrea Ghez
strings.summary: Andrea Ghez used high-resolution infrared observations to follow stars near the Galactic center, building key evidence with her team for a supermassive compact object there. Using the Keck telescopes and adaptive optics, she measured stellar orbits and tested relativistic effects in strong gravity. She and Reinhard Genzel shared half of the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics; the other half went to Roger Penrose.
strings.coverageNote: Research checked through 13 November 2026; selected milestones extend to 2020. This is not a daily news archive. Shared achievements are credited to collaborators and teams.
strings.influence.rationale: Studied stars at the Galactic Center with high-resolution astronomical observations, providing important evidence for a supermassive black hole.

strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Stellar orbits reveal a compact object
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Long-term stellar tracking constrained the central object's mass and size.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Observational tests of relativity
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Used stellar motions and spectra, including those of S0-2, to test general relativity near the Galactic center.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Nobel Prize in Physics
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Shared half the prize with Genzel for discovery of a supermassive compact object at the Galactic center.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: S0-2 relativistic redshift
strings.timeline.event-2.text: The team published redshift measurements near the central object that agreed with general relativity.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Refined central-object measurements
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Published stellar-orbit measurements of the Galactic center's mass and distance with her team.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: MacArthur Fellowship
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Recognized for sustained high-resolution studies of the Galactic center.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Joined UCLA faculty
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Joined the University of California, Los Angeles and developed a long-term Galactic-center program.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Completed Caltech doctorate
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Earned her doctorate through work on high-resolution astronomical observations.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: MIT physics degree
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Completed undergraduate physics before graduate study at Caltech.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Born in New York
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Born in New York City and grew up in Chicago.
